audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph Ammonite diplomatic humiliation and Aramean war, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed against 2 Samuel 10 for bereavement diplomacy, espionage fear, shaving and garment exposure, recovery privacy, mercenary hiring, city defense, mutual aid, war theology, casualty numbers, forced peace, and servitude.

verses.restored: After this Nahash king of Ammonites died, and his son reigned in his place.

David said, I will show covenant-kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me. David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. David's servants came to land of Ammonites to Hanun to comfort him.
Ammonite officials said to Hanun, Does David honor your father in your eyes by sending comforters? Have his servants not come to search, overthrow, and spy out land?
Hanun took David's servants, shaved them, cut garments in middle near buttocks, and sent them away.
People went and told David concerning men. He sent to meet them, for men were greatly humiliated. King said, Stay at Jericho until your beards grow, then return.
Ammonites saw they had made themselves odious to David; Hanun and Ammonites sent one thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, Aram-maacah, and Zobah.
They hired thirty-two thousand chariots/forces and king of Maacah with people; they came and camped before Medeba. Ammonites gathered from cities and came for battle.
David heard and sent Joab and all army of mighty warriors.
Ammonites came out and arranged battle at city gate, while kings who came were separately in field.
Joab saw battle was against him front and rear; he chose from best of Israel and arranged them against Arameans.
Rest of people he gave into hand of Abishai his brother, and they arranged against Ammonites.
He said, If Arameans are too strong for me, you shall rescue me; if Ammonites too strong for you, I will rescue you.
Be strong, and let us strengthen ourselves for our people and cities of our Divine; may YHWH do what is good in the eyes.
Joab and people with him approached Arameans for battle, and they fled before him.
Ammonites saw Arameans fled and also fled before Abishai his brother and entered city. Joab came to Jerusalem.
Arameans saw they were defeated before Israel, sent messengers, and brought Arameans beyond river; Shophach commander of Hadadezer's army led them.
It was told David; he gathered all Israel, crossed Jordan, came to them, and arranged battle. David arranged against Arameans, and they fought him.
Arameans fled before Israel; David killed seven thousand chariot fighters and forty thousand foot soldiers and put Shophach commander to death.
Servants of Hadadezer saw they were defeated before Israel, made peace with David, and served him. Arameans were unwilling to help Ammonites again.

translation_notes: The chapter begins with grief diplomacy. Security concerns about espionage can be understandable, but fear does not justify abuse of envoys.
Shaving and cutting garments to expose buttocks is sexualized and gendered humiliation. It must not be treated as comedy or proof that masculinity depends on hair and clothing.
David gives the men privacy and time before public return, a constructive response to humiliation, though their own wishes are not recorded.
'Made themselves odious' describes a damaged political relationship and must not become an ethnic slur against Ammonites.
Hiring allied forces shows the economics of war; silver, transport, animals, and soldiers are mobilized through elite decisions.
Joab's mutual-support plan is tactically constructive but does not sanctify the war or erase civilians at Medeba and city gates.
The prayer that YHWH do what is good leaves outcome open; it is not proof every subsequent killing is Divine will.
Forty-seven thousand reported deaths are human catastrophe and the numbers differ from 2 Samuel 10.
Peace after overwhelming defeat and ensuing service to David are coerced imperial terms, not free reconciliation.
safety_note: Do not mock sexualized humiliation, define manhood through beards, demonize Ammonites or Arameans, glorify mercenary war, or call forced submission peace. Center bereavement, bodily dignity, recovery privacy, civilian impact, and the humanity behind casualty totals.
